newsitem.title: USA: Japan urges resumption of aviation talks with U.S.
newsitem.headline: Japan urges resumption of aviation talks with U.S.

text.p: Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda Wednesday urged the United States to resume talks to settle a dispute over civil aviation rights without any preconditions, a Japanese spokesman said.

The aviation dispute was one of a number of issues Ikeda discussed with Secretary of State Warren Christopher at a meeting in Washington on Wednesday, Ikeda spokesman Hiroshi Hashimoto told reporters following the meeting.
The two men also talked about a dispute over a 1994 trade agreement on insurance deregulation in Japan and negotiations taking place this week in Tokyo, Hashimoto said.
Hashimoto said both Ikeda and Christopher expressed a desire to resolve the two trade disputes, but no agreements were reached.

Negotiations on aviation rights and a 1952 agreement that Japan says favors the United States broke down last month. Washington, which would like an "open skies" agreement with Japan, blamed Tokyo for blocking resolution of the dispute. Hashimoto said that Ikeda told Christopher that talks should resume but that there should be no preconditions for the discussions.
Hashimoto said Ikeda told Christopher he hopes the two sides could find a "mutually agreeable" solution to the insurance issue and U.S. concerns that Tokyo was about to reneg on the 1994 agreement.

Ikeda also brought up a supercomputer antidumping case now pending before the International Trade Commission and the Commerce Department. The case involves an antidumping complaint by U.S. supercomputer maker Cray Research, a unit of Silicon Graphics Inc, against NEC Corp about a supercomputer purchase by the University Corporation for Atmospheric Research.
Hashimoto said Ikeda told Christopher that Japan was watching the case closely and urged a "fair and open" process.
